name: Liberal democracy
summary: Liberal democracy is a form of government that joins popular rule through free, competitive elections with liberal constitutionalism: rulers hold power by the consent of the governed but are constitutionally bound to respect individual and minority rights. Its defining accounts name universal suffrage, secret ballots and freedom to form parties; guarantees of speech, press, conscience, religion, assembly and property; equality before the law; and separated powers, an independent judiciary and the rule of law that limit what majorities and executives may do. It rests on claims of human equality and universal natural rights going back to Locke, and its adherents divide, as liberal right and liberal left, over how far the state should act in the economy.
scope: Liberal democracy as its defining reference and scholarly accounts set it out: the Gale encyclopedia entry (Watson), Fareed Zakaria's 'The Rise of Illiberal Democracy', Marc Plattner's Journal of Democracy essays, the introduction to Fukuyama's The End of History and the Last Man, and the V-Dem codebook's definition of the liberal democracy index, with Madison's Federalist No. 10, which Plattner names as its vision. It covers the regime type and the principles those sources make part of it, not the policies of particular liberal democratic governments or parties, nor classical liberalism, constitutional liberalism or pluralist democracy as separate ideologies. Policy questions the sources leave open are null; where Gale records the liberal right and liberal left dividing, the answer is a split.

notes: Later pass under rules 5 (claude-opus-5-5, 2026-11-10). The first pass rested on Wikipedia (s1, s5), on the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (s3), which no defining source makes liberal democracy's own text, and on the SEP entry on democracy (s2), which never names liberal democracy; it also recorded many policy questions as 0. Those answers are nulled, each with its reviewHistory, and only positions the defining accounts state are kept. Liberal democracy defines a regime type, so its sources are silent on most economic, social, ecological, technological and foreign-policy statements; the Gale entry records the liberal right and liberal left dividing on state action in the economy, answered as splits only where the statement is about that division. Liberal democracy is the constitutional order of many states, but none makes it a ruling party's doctrine in the sense of PROMPT.md section 3, so no state's record is used and every source is words. Themes searched: government and elections (Gale, Zakaria, Plattner, V-Dem electoral and liberal components, Federalist No. 10), liberty and civil rights (V-Dem civil liberty indicators), religion (V-Dem freedom of religion, Zakaria), economy (Fukuyama, Gale, Zakaria), world (Zakaria and Fukuyama on the liberal peace; Plattner's 'Globalization and Self-Government' was read but states Plattner's own argument, not tenets of liberal democracy, so it is not cited). Not reachable: Merkel's 'Embedded and Defective Democracies' (EconStor returned a bot check), Fukuyama's 1989 essay (the DTIC copy returned 403; other copies are third-party uploads), Diamond's Kellogg working papers (404) and his 1996 Journal of Democracy essay (Project MUSE paywall). Militant democracy and party bans were searched for in the defining sources and not found, so ban-extremist-parties is null.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: V-Dem's liberal component includes secure private property rights, defined as the right to acquire, possess, inherit and sell property, including land.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Freedom of religion in V-Dem's liberal component includes the right to change religion, and Gale lists freedom of conscience and religion among the guarantees.

bound-labor.rationale: V-Dem's liberal component includes freedom from servitude and forced labor for men and women.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Plattner describes populists appealing to the majority directly without regard for checks and balances as a threat to liberal democracy, and Gale makes freedom to form parties a minimum feature.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Fukuyama places modern liberal democracy and technologically driven capitalism together at the end of a directional history of human societies.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Gale requires effective guarantees of freedom of speech and press and of freedom to engage in one's own pursuits.

central-planning.rationale: Fukuyama argues that the logic of modern science leads to capitalism rather than socialism as the economic counterpart of liberal democracy.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Fukuyama replaces the Marxist account with Hegel's struggle for recognition as the motor of history leading to liberal democracy.

clerical-rule.rationale: Fukuyama counts theocracy among the more primitive forms of rule that liberal democracy supersedes, and Zakaria lists separation of church and state among its tenets.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Gale entry defines liberal democracy as government in which people consent to their rulers, following Locke's argument that legitimate authority arises only from consent.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: V-Dem's liberal principle protects individual and minority rights against the tyranny of the majority through an independent judiciary, and Plattner describes liberal democracy as limiting the day-to-day rule of the majority.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Gale sets out both sides inside liberal democracy: Tocqueville's heirs fear government taking over what people do for themselves, while the liberal left sees administrative state power as necessary for social justice.

decide-locally.rationale: Zakaria argues that unchecked centralization has been the enemy of liberal democracy and that strong regional and local institutions sustain it; the other defining sources do not discuss it.

democracy-best.rationale: Fukuyama argues that the ideal of liberal democracy cannot be improved on, and Plattner that voters must be convinced of its superiority to all alternatives; Zakaria warns that elections without liberal protections can do harm.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Zakaria and Plattner both hold that free elections without the rule of law and protected rights make an illiberal democracy, not a liberal one.

democratic-peace.rationale: Fukuyama holds that liberal democracies do not behave imperialistically toward one another, so a world of them has less reason for war; Zakaria warns that democratizing states without constitutional liberalism go to war more often.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Liberal democracy guarantees individual and minority rights and equal treatment before the law for all citizens, which a class dictatorship denies (Gale).

direct-action.rationale: In Gale's account change comes through frequent elections in which parties compete to form a government that alters the laws.

direct-votes.rationale: Gale describes modern democracy as indirect rule through elected representatives, and Madison's Federalist No. 10, which Plattner treats as the vision of liberal democracy, prefers representation to pure democracy.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Gale requires equal treatment before the law, and V-Dem's liberal component measures access to justice and property rights for women and men alike.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Gale grounds legitimate political authority in the consent of the governed, the principle Locke and the Declaration of Independence set out.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Gale says liberal democracy requires freedom from politics and would be totalitarian if citizens were constantly occupied by obligations to the state.

economic-freedom.rationale: Zakaria says the factors most closely associated with full liberal democracies are capitalism, a bourgeoisie and high income, and Gale records the liberal right backing markets as a check on state power; Gale's liberal left sees state power as a positive good.

elective-rulers.rationale: V-Dem's electoral core requires that elections affect the composition of the chief executive.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Zakaria argues that states suspending constitutional rights in crises have usually produced neither order nor good government, while conceding exceptions in emergencies such as war.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Zakaria says constitutional liberalism requires a basic law limiting government's powers to secure natural rights, and V-Dem names constitutionally protected civil liberties; Gale notes the guarantees may also be unwritten shared understandings.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Gale says all liberal democracies recognise human freedom and political equality, and lists equal treatment before the law among the minimum guarantees.

every-country-ready-for-democracy.rationale: Gale says liberal democratic principles cannot be implemented universally or immediately, and Zakaria that elections without a constitutional liberal background can be a false step.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: V-Dem measures freedom from political killings within the liberal component, and Plattner names Duterte's extrajudicial killings of drug dealers among his outrageously illiberal actions.

free-trade-promotes-peace.rationale: Zakaria argues that the democratic peace is a liberal peace, resting partly on free trade, which makes war costly and cooperation useful.

independent-unions.rationale: V-Dem's freedom of association index, part of liberal democracy's electoral core, asks whether civil society organisations can form and operate freely and without repression.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Plattner says liberal democracy rests on universal principles, and Gale that its principles are universal even if they cannot be implemented everywhere at once; Zakaria allows different frameworks within it.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Zakaria describes democratization in parts of the Islamic world bringing theocratic politics as a loss of liberalism, and names separation of church and state as a liberal tenet.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Rule by a single leading party contradicts liberal democracy's requirement, in Gale, that every party be free to present its views and form a government.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Fukuyama pairs liberal democracy with liberal economics, saying the free market has produced unprecedented prosperity, while Gale records the liberal left seeking state power to tame the market.

minority-veto.rationale: Gale says liberal democratic governments can alter and enforce laws to suit the majority's preferences within limits, and Plattner says liberal democracy ultimately depends on the will of the majority.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Gale traces liberal democracy through England's limited monarchy, where sovereignty rested on a compact between the people's representatives in parliament and the monarch.

natural-rulers.rationale: The Gale entry grounds liberal democracy in Locke's premise that people are by nature political equals and that no one is good enough to rule another without consent.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Gale makes secret ballots and frequent regular elections, with parties free to form a government, minimum features of liberal democracy.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Gale entry lists broad freedom to form parties, each free to present its views and form a government, among the minimum features of liberal democracy.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation through freely formed political parties competing in elections is among Gale's minimum features of liberal democracy.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Gale presents the Glorious Revolution, which ended the royal power to suspend laws and required free elections for parliament, as a milestone of liberal democracy.

party-controls-media.rationale: V-Dem counts freedom of expression and an independent media presenting alternative views as part of the electoral core of liberal democracy, and Gale lists effective guarantees of press freedom.

person-over-state.rationale: Gale says government remains legitimate only so long as it protects individuals' natural rights, and Zakaria describes the tradition as protecting individual autonomy and dignity against coercion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: V-Dem's liberal component measures rigorous and impartial public administration under transparent laws, the opposite of authority resting on personal oaths.

population-transfer.rationale: Gale lists effective guarantees of minority rights and participation by ethnic and religious minorities among the minimum features of liberal democracy.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: V-Dem's liberal component measures transparent laws with predictable enforcement and impartial administration, and Zakaria contrasts the rule of law with government by presidential decree.

property-franchise.rationale: Gale requires participation by adult citizens including economic minorities, and V-Dem's electoral core requires extensive suffrage; Zakaria calls the restricted-franchise states of the 19th century liberal autocracies, not democracies.

property-fundamental.rationale: Zakaria lists property among the basic liberties of liberal democracy and V-Dem counts secure property rights in its liberal component; Zakaria also notes that Sweden curtails property rights and is still a democracy.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Gale requires effective guarantees of freedom of speech, conscience and religion, and V-Dem's freedom of religion covers public practice without restriction by public authorities.

racial-franchise.rationale: Gale lists widespread participation by adult citizens, explicitly including racial and ethnic minorities, as a minimum feature of liberal democracy.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Gale requires equal treatment before the law and presents the civil rights movement as resting on liberal understandings of natural rights.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Gale records a split within liberal democracy: the liberal right favours the market and limited government, while the liberal left sees state power as necessary to tame the worst effects of the marketplace.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: Liberal democracy, in Gale's account, includes ethnic minorities in political participation and guarantees their rights.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Gale says government stays legitimate only so long as it protects citizens' natural rights, and presents Locke's account of the Glorious Revolution as a founding theory.

restrict-conversion.rationale: V-Dem's freedom of religion indicator, part of the liberal component, includes the right to change one's religion and to proselytise peacefully without restriction.

rule-by-example.rationale: Zakaria says the Western model is symbolised by the impartial judge, resting on the rule of law rather than on rulers.

separate-church-state.rationale: Zakaria lists separation of church and state among the guarantees of constitutional liberalism, though he also notes that England keeps an established religion.

separated-powers.rationale: Every defining account names it: Gale lists separation of powers among the minimum features, Zakaria defines liberal democracy by a separation of powers, and V-Dem by effective checks and balances.

single-common-good.rationale: Plattner says the Madisonian pluralism of competing interests fits liberal-democratic politics, which balances majority rule with individual and minority rights.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Gale defines liberal democracy by rulers constitutionally constrained to respect rights, and Zakaria traces it to the barons forcing the king to abide by the law of the land.

state-harmful.rationale: Liberal democracy is a system of government whose energetic but constitutionally constrained state protects rights, as Gale describes the American founding.

strong-leader.rationale: V-Dem's liberal model judges democracy by the limits placed on executive power, and Zakaria treats presidents who bypass parliaments by decree as the mark of illiberal democracy.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: V-Dem's freedom of religion indicator scores lowest where religious leaders are appointed by and subject to public authorities.

suppress-opposition.rationale: V-Dem's liberal democracy index builds on freedom of association: opposition parties allowed to form and compete, and civil society organisations free to form and operate.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: Freedom from torture by state agents is one of the physical integrity rights V-Dem's liberal component measures.

total-state.rationale: Gale says liberal democracy requires freedom from politics and would be totalitarian rather than liberal if citizens were constantly occupied by obligations to the state.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Gale names Nazism and communism together as the illiberal ideologies that challenged liberal democracy, and Zakaria groups Nazi Germany, Soviet Russia and Maoist China as the century's worst strong states.

universal-morality.rationale: Plattner holds that liberal democracy is based on universal principles, and Gale that its principles of freedom and equality are universal natural rights.

vanguard-party.rationale: Gale counts communism among the illiberal ideologies that challenged liberal democracy and requires every party to be free to form a government.

women-must-cover.rationale: Zakaria cites Iran's elected parliament imposing restrictions on dress as an example of diminishing liberty in an illiberal democracy.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: V-Dem's liberal component measures women's right to acquire, possess, inherit and sell private property, including land, alongside men's.

women-suffrage.rationale: Gale presents women's suffrage as resting on embedded liberal understandings of natural rights, and V-Dem's electoral core requires extensive suffrage.

workers-councils.rationale: Gale describes liberal democracy as popular rule through elected representatives, with parties free to compete and form a government.
